reader.title: Lynching of Archie Walker
bases: The only report says the citizens of Waco, Miss., took Archie Walker and hanged him to a tree over an alleged attempted outrage (A1).

A1 reports that 'the citizens' of Waco, a group with no stated legal authority, seized and hanged Walker for an alleged attempted outrage, which meets the standard definition; the account rests on one brief wire item with no date, detail or follow-up (A1).
Only one brief telegraphic item was found, with no local, follow-up or independent report (A1).

summary.text: The lynching of Archie Walker was the hanging of a Black man by "the citizens of Waco," Mississippi, reported in late September 1881.
Walker was accused of attempting to "outrage" the daughter of a man identified as Capt. Lee, and he was hanged to a tree.
The episode is known from a single one-sentence telegraphic item.
According to the brief, the citizens of Waco, Miss., took Archie Walker, whom it called "a negro," and hanged him to a tree.
The item gave the reason as an attempt to "outrage the daughter of Capt. Lee," stating the accusation as fact rather than as a charge.
It did not give the date of the hanging, where Walker was seized, whether he had been arrested, how many people took part, or the time of day.
Neither Capt. Lee nor his daughter was further identified, and no county was named.
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage.
The Morning Journal and Courier printed the item on September 30, 1881, on page 3 under the heading "Telegraphic Jottings."
There it ran as one unheadlined sentence between a note on a rowing match and a note that the English minister had postponed his departure for Washington.
The paper offered no comment on the hanging and attributed the act to "the citizens" of the town rather than to a mob.
No other paper carrying the story, and no local Mississippi account, was found for September and October 1881.

accounts.label: Wire report
accounts.gist: The citizens of Waco, Miss., took Archie Walker, who it says attempted to outrage Capt. Lee's daughter, and hanged him to a tree.

framing.detail: A single unheadlined sentence under 'Telegraphic Jottings', between items on a rowing match and a diplomat's travel, that states the accusation as fact ('who attempted to outrage') and offers no comment.

record_check.dossier: The date of the hanging is not stated; the only report ran on 1881-09-30, so the act was on or before that date.
No county is named; the report gives only Waco, Miss.
The report as written meets the definition (a group, 'the citizens', hanged him over an alleged crime); the remaining doubt is about the evidence, a single unsourced brief, not the definition.
Not reported; the item says only that the citizens 'took' Walker.
